hypotheses.claim: Because all size=100 and uniform-spatial/eccentric-depot/loose-capacity regimes show exhausted_instances (LNS iterations truncated by the 500 ms deadline) and their vbs_rel_gap_pct is ~-20%, the binding constraint is iteration throughput at large n, not local-optimum quality. A ruin score that (a) scales the rank-power exponent with iter_frac and stagnation_ratio, (b) down-weights per-node evaluation cost via a distance-gated coarse candidate set (O(n) instead of O(n^2) relatedness), and (c) makes the recreate hook prefer geometrically coherent (angular-sector / heavy-load) insertions rather than pure detour-minimum, will increase completed LNS iterations per 500 ms on size=100 instances and thus lower mean objective vs the current SBS 16.1100 without regressing n<=64 cases.

next_search_advice.direction: Regime-adaptive dual-hook LNS: make `score_ruin_nodes` cost-per-iteration aware and `score_recreate_action` regime-conditioned so that large-n (size=100), uniform-spatial, eccentric-depot, loose-capacity instances get geometric/angular-cluster ruin with cheaper per-node scoring, while small-n instances get aggressive worst-cost removal.
